anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

bible_refs.note: Quoted sense: work while it is day; night comes when no one can work.

pass_a_gloss: For Jews partake of them raw, leaning on the wordings of the writings alone; but if through the Spirit they see the true circumcision, for example, and the true sabbath, and they work while it is day before the night comes, when no longer no one can work, they already eat the saying boiled through the Spirit.
pass_b_english: [For the Jews partake of them raw, leaning on the words of the scriptures alone. But if through the Spirit they see the true circumcision, for example, and the true sabbath, and they work while it is day before the night comes, when no one can work any longer, they already eat the saying boiled through the Spirit.]
source_text: Ἰουδαῖοι μὲν γὰρ ὠμῶν μεταλαμβάνουσιν αὐτῶν, μόναις ταῖς λέξεσιν ἐπερειδόμενοι τῶν|| [γραφῶν· εἰ δὲ διὰ τοῦ πν(εύματο)ς ὁρῶσι τὴν ἀληθῆ περιτομήν, εἰ τύχοι, καὶ τὸ ἀληθινὸν σάββατον, καὶ ἐργάζονται ἕως ἡμέρα ἐστὶν πρὶν ἐλθεῖν τὴν νύκτα, ὅτε οὐκέτι οὐδεὶς δύναται ἐργάζεσθαι, ἤδη διὰ τοῦ πν(εύματο)ς ἡψημένον ἐσθίουσι τὸ ῥητόν.]
